check.title: AI check · VegvisAI
check.description: Free check of how a website looks to AI assistants: robots.txt, sitemap, schema.org, llms.txt, ai-catalog.json and text that resembles prompt injection.
check.intro: How does your website look to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and local language models? The check reads only public files, like a search engine does, and respects robots.txt.
check.whatIntro: The check has five yardsticks: business, public body, organisation (NGO, association), political party and news medium. Most of it is the same for all; only the content part differs. The yardstick is detected from schema.org on the pages, the domain (for example kommune.no) or the open index of public services. You can also choose it yourself.
check.row1: robots.txt lets in the AI bots that fetch pages when someone asks (15), and the training bots (5). Blocking only training can be a deliberate choice
check.row2: A sitemap exists, and at most half of the pages are dated more than two years back
check.row3: Every page has its own title; every page has a meta description
check.row4: The business or body is described with schema.org (Organization, LocalBusiness, GovernmentOrganization, NGO, PoliticalParty and the like)
check.row5: The pages show at least 300 characters of text without JavaScript; the language is declared; every page has a main heading
check.row6: Products or services have structured data with name, price and currency (and availability for goods)
check.row7: Content pages are marked with a type (Article, WebPage, Service, Event and the like) and a date (published or changed)
check.row8: The front page links to the key pages: services, contact and about (public body); work, membership, contact and about (organisation); party programme, policy, representatives and contact (party); about, contact and editorial standards (medium)
check.row9: /llms.txt (2; contested, Google says it can be ignored) and /.well-known/ai-catalog.json valid by the AI Catalog specification (5)
check.note1: Checks that do not apply, such as prices on a site without prices, do not count, and the total is scaled to 100. If the front page does not answer, no score is given: the site is not measured. The check also looks for text that resembles instructions to AI assistants (prompt injection), also in hidden text. Such findings do not cost points, but come first among the actions. A few zero-width characters, which often come from copy and paste, count as low risk.
check.note2: The check also lists what the site has open for AI beyond the pages: news feeds, calendar, search and actions in schema.org, open data, OpenAPI and MCP. This gives no points yet.
check.note3: We keep no log of the addresses that are checked, and we use no cookies. The check does not run JavaScript; content that is only made in the browser is not seen. That is also how many AI agents read web pages.
check.checking: Checking … this takes 5–15 seconds, because we wait a little between each request to the site.
check.warnTitle: Pattern matches that resemble instructions to AI
check.warnText: Some text on the site resembles patterns often used to give instructions to AI assistants. A match says nothing about intent. The text is shown here as a quote and is not followed.
check.keyH2: Key pages from the front page
check.openNote: This is what an AI agent can use directly, beyond reading the pages. It gives no points yet, but shows what is possible.
check.footer: Time: {time}. A sample, not a full review.
check.noteOthers: Other free checks measure more technical details for developers, for example Cloudflare's isitagentready.com. This check adds yardsticks for public bodies, organisations, parties and news media, the scan for hidden instructions, plain advice, and a ready AI business card. What matters most is still your own clear website; a free Google Business Profile helps too.

register.title: Register your business · VegvisAI
register.description: Register your business in the open guide. We read the AI business card on your own domain and check it in a public register where we can. Free, and ranking cannot be bought.
register.intro: Does your business have an AI business card on its own website? Then it can be registered in the open guide, so AI assistants that do not know you yet can find their way to your card. It is free, and placement cannot be bought.
register.noCard: No business card yet? Make one here in about fifteen minutes, and run the AI check on your website first.
register.labelOther: Not needed outside Norway, the EU and the UK
register.labelGB: Company number (optional; it must be in your card as identifier with propertyID companyNumber)
register.labelEU: VAT number (optional; it must be in your card as vatID)
register.consent: I have the right to register this business. (Whether the entry is shared openly under ODbL and DbCL is chosen on the business's own website, in ai-catalog.json; the generator adds it. Without it the business is found in the guide, but not in the open export.)
register.step1: We read /.well-known/ai-catalog.json and the business card on your own domain.
register.step2: Norwegian businesses: we check the organisation number in Enhetsregisteret, without bankruptcy or winding-up. EU businesses: we check the VAT number in your card (schema.org vatID) in the EU register VIES. UK businesses: the company number is checked in Companies House. Other countries: only the domain is checked.
register.step3: The website in the register or in your card must point to the same domain. If not, a person looks at it.
register.step4: We look for hidden instructions to AI in the card.
register.step5: At the start, a person reviews every new entry before it is shown. You can check the status below.
register.privacy: We do not ask for your email and keep no personal data from the form. Every listing, change and removal is in the public changelog. We re-check entries every week; if the card is gone, the entry is removed. Read how the guide chooses results.
register.statusLabel: Organisation number, VAT number with country code (DE123456789) or web:domain
register.sending: Reading the business card and checking the register …

status.pending: Received. A person reviews the entry before it is shown.

create.title: Make an AI business card · VegvisAI
create.description: Answer a few questions and get a business card that AI assistants understand: an HTML page with schema.org, llms.txt and ai-catalog.json. Everything happens in your browser; nothing is stored.
create.test: Technical test. Not a launch. Everything happens in your browser: we do not see what you type, and nothing is stored.
create.intro: Answer the questions and you get three files that make your business understandable for ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and local language models. You put them on your own website; you own them, and we keep no copy.
create.companyNumberHelp: Needed to be verified when you register in the guide.
create.vatIdHelp: Needed to be verified in the EU register VIES when you register in the guide.
create.lookupHelp: Optional. Fetches name and address from Enhetsregisteret.
create.lookupBankrupt: The entity is registered as bankrupt or being wound up.

create.licence: Share our business card openly in the VegvisAI index
create.licenceHelp: Under the open licences ODbL (the index) and DbCL (your entry), so other open guides can use it too. The choice is written into ai-catalog.json on your own website; only you can give or remove it. Copies others have already downloaded cannot be recalled. Without it you are still found in the VegvisAI guide, but not in the open export.
